atoms.b: Cities such as Rome strive to preserve ancient monuments. For example, the Colosseum is an iconic ((++Roman Tudor)) amphitheatre that hosted gladiator fights and was built almost 2,000 years ago.

Italy’s history is one of the main reasons it attracts millions of ((++tourists attractions)) each year. Tourism contributes to around 10% of Italy’s total GDP, making it one of the country’s most important industries.

hint.label: GDP
hint.text: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product. It is a measure of the total amount of money made from everything a country produces and all the services it provides.

hint.label: Did you know?
hint.sound: The Olive Tree of Vooves is one of the oldest olive trees in the world. It is located on the island of Crete in Greece and is around 4,000 years old!
text: The Olive Tree of Vouves is one of the oldest olive trees in the world. It is located on the island of Crete in Greece and is around 4,000 years old!

atoms.a: Greece is well known for its delicious olives.
Olive trees thrive here as cool sea air from the Mediterranean helps to prevent extreme temperatures.
Olive trees have adapted to have waxy leaves, which help them to retain water during hot summers.
As a result, olives and olive oil have been the cornerstone of the Mediterranean diet for millennia.

atoms.b: Home to some of Europe’s most diverse cultures and landscapes, the Balkans are a region in Southern Europe, located ((++east west)) of the Adriatic Sea.
Unfortunately, the population here is declining rapidly. Several Balkan nations have some of the fastest-declining ((++populations temperatures)) globally.
For example, it is predicted that Bosnia and Herzegovina will ((++lose gain)) 55% of its population by 2070.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The Iberian Peninsular forms the other part of Southern Europe. It is made up of Portugal and Spain and is the westernmost part of the European continent.

The Tabernas Desert in the south of Spain is considered Europe’s only true desert, despite having an area of just 150 km². Its surrounding mountains block rain clouds from the Mediterranean Sea, which keeps the climate dry.
The climate differs drastically in the north of Spain. This area is known as Green Spain due to its lush, green landscape. Unlike the Tabernas, the north of Spain is characterised by high rainfall.

atoms.a: Which two countries make up the Iberian Peninsula?
What is a key factor that keeps the climate dry in the Tabernas Desert?
b: ++Mountains that block rain clouds from reaching the region.
Trees that catch rainfall and keep the ground dry.
The sea is too far from the desert for it to rain.

atoms.a: Why is the north of Spain known as Green Spain?
b: ++Green Spain has a lush, green landscape.
Green Spain is filled with rainforests.
Green Spain is known for its many marshes.
